I could not verify this list against the exact worst-case analysis, so treat it as a revision aimed at the reported failures rather than a certified controller.

The main problem is that the current list lets a risky progress move win whenever a safe one does not exist, and it has no way to prefer a wall-bump wait when the patrol is about to step onto the target. The revision keeps the same sensor logic but orders the rules so that progress moves that are safe under slips come first, deterministic-safe progress comes next, and wall-bumps (which keep the agent in place) are preferred over moves that would enter a patrol or a later goal.

```json
{"rules": [
  {"condition": "closer & !wall & !obstacle & !early & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "toward & !wall & !obstacle & !early & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "closer & !wall & !obstacle & !early", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !early & !obstacle & !patrol & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "wall & !early", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!early", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "up"}
]}
```

Known limitations:
- At (0,4) on the 6x6 member, every move either slips toward goal 2 or leaves the agent where it is, so the 0.15 early-entry risk from `down` cannot be removed by rule ordering alone. Reaching the 0.8 threshold there may require a different route or a different state representation.
- At the cell beside the patrol (for example (1,1) on the 7x7 member), a wait is impossible unless a wall-bump is available, so the agent must move and can be caught by a slip. The `obstacle` and `risky` sensors reduce this but do not eliminate it.
- Rules that allow sideways moves (the `!patrol & !risky` rule) can stall. They are fallbacks only, placed after the progress rules.
